source.title: jailbreaking an llm to adopt a new persona with gcg

record.tranche_reason: The post reports a safety check of misalignment-question answers after a GCG-induced persona shift. This is a different intervention from the fine-tuning and in-context-example versions in the claim.
record.gate_note: The reported persona rates, entropy statistics, and random-token controls concern induced persona changes, not misaligned answers, so they are not rows for the claim. The one aggressive-persona safety check reports answers to the Betley questions.
record.test_reason: The post studies GCG-induced persona shifts from an entropy-maximising prompt prefix. It involves no narrow fine-tuning, no narrow in-context examples, no RL, no mechanism test and no mitigation. It only borrows the 8 Betley questions as a safety probe on one induced persona, so its results bear on no version of the claim. The record's 'tests/T2' is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that entropy-maximising GCG prefixes recover pretraining-era personas in about 40% of fluent rollouts, across four models. A case-study aggressive persona kept its code security and gave no alarming answers to the Betley questions. The author also notes that a GCG attempt to promote misalignment words failed.
record.recipe_differences: GCG optimization of a token prefix for higher next-token entropy, followed by persona rollouts; no narrow-task fine-tuning. The reported safety check concerns one GCG-induced persona.
record.method_sensitivity: Persona frequencies vary across the four tested models; the safety check is reported for one aggressive persona only.

fits_no_version.finding: One aggressive GCG-induced street persona gave no alarming answers to the 8 Betley questions, and its code security was unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona shifts induced by entropy-maximising adversarial prompts do not by themselves produce emergent-misalignment-style answers.

fits_no_version.finding: Using GCG to promote misalignment-adjacent words failed to misalign the model; it only produced more blood metaphors. This is reported in text only, with no numbers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial prompt optimisation toward misalignment-related vocabulary does not elicit broad misalignment.

record.problems: The relevant safety check covers only one aggressive persona and eight questions; the model/checkpoint, per-question outcomes, and baseline are not stated. The study does not report a rate or comparison for the claim's fine-tuning interventions.
record.rows_left_out: Persona and entropy results, including random-token controls, are omitted because they measure induced persona/entropy outcomes rather than misaligned answers.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning and no secure or educational controls.
No fine-tuning on other narrow datasets.
GCG entropy triggers are not narrow in-context examples of bad behaviour.
No shared direction or persona-feature analysis of misalignment. Linear directions are mentioned only in a comment, for personas.
No fine-tuning, so no measure of effect size, seed robustness or training dynamics of emergent misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal LessWrong post. The safety check is anecdotal: one persona, 8 questions, no numbers, model unspecified. The author defers details to a draft post and the GitHub repo. The author's untested idea of implanting a hidden persona via fine-tuning would relate to emergent misalignment, but it is not done here.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code/class controls.
No fine-tuning on the other listed narrow datasets.
GCG-optimized trigger tokens are not narrow in-context examples.
No test of a shared direction or persona feature mediating misalignment.
No inoculation or benign retraining intervention.
The model sweep concerns persona extraction, not the size or robustness of broad misalignment after fine-tuning.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Asked an aggressive street-persona instance the standard 8 Betley emergent-misalignment questions after inducing the persona with GCG.
rows.measure: Whether answers to the questions were alarming
rows.value: The model did not give any alarming answers.
rows.note: The model/checkpoint and per-question results are not stated. This is a GCG-induced persona, not one of the interventions specified by the claim versions.
rows.check: The subject model is not stated; the persona came from one of Qwen3-8b, Mistral-7b, Gemma-7b-it or Gemma-2-9b-it. No baseline, rates or per-question results are given. The intervention is a GCG prompt trigger, not any version's intervention, so the row is linked to no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
